These are spaces of the score track values 0 through 5, as denoted at the end of the name. All countries begin with a score of 0, so 6 country score token will begin in the score_0 space. These score tokens are advanced to further spaces of the score track as the game progresses, during the taxation action. These score values correspond to an x0 multiplier when calculating victory points (this multiplier is applied to the total value of stocks of a given country held by each player).

LR followed by number followed by space should be interpreted as a space in land region of the given number where land armies can be placed. If the land region is neutral, control flags can also be placed there when a country's land armies abandon it, to denote ownership. If the land region is assigned to a country at the beginning of the game, no flags can be placed there, only land armies. In the event that there are more armies/flags to be placed on that region than there are spaces for them, place the excess units/flag in contact with an already occupied space of that region. Regions have different number of such spaces simply due to physical limiations of the board, and each such space in the region has the exact same name. It doesn't matter which of these same-numbered spaces are chosen to use first.

SR followed by number followed by space should be interpreted as a space in sea region of the given number where fleets or control flags can be placed. In the event that there are more fleets/flags to be placed on that region than there are spaces for them, place the excess fleets/flags in contact with the an already occupied space of that region. Each such space in a single region has the exact same name. It doesn't matter which of these same-numbered spaces are chosen to use first.

LR followed by a number followed by land_f indicates a space for a region's land factory. Only non-neutral regions have spaces for land or sea factories. When a country is building a factory, the player controlling it should choose one of the land or sea factory slots in the original territory of that country.

LR followed by a number followed by sea_f indicates a space for a region's sea factory. Only non-neutral regions have spaces for land or sea factories. When a country is building a factory, the player controlling it should choose one of the land or sea factory slots in the original territory of that country.

Newly built fleets are placed in ports. While in a port, a fleet participates in any combat in that land region just like an army. Fleets can also enter ports controlled by their country from a sea region, but only from the sea region connected to that port.
